Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN) -- A 4-year-old Ohio girl who vanished more than three weeks ago was found alive and in good condition, halfway across the country in southern California, authorities said. Haylee Donathan was found with her mother and her mother's boyfriend, fugitive sex offender Robbie Potter. Haylee Donathan, her mother Candace Watson and Robbie Potter were discovered hiding for the past week at The Morning Star Ranch, a retreat in Valley Center, near San Diego, said Peter Elliott, United States Marshal for the Northern District of Ohio. Potter is a registered sex offender, officials said. He was being sought by the U.S. Marshal's Service. Late Tuesday Haylee was in the custody of a children's protective services agency in the San Diego County area, Elliott said. She was doing well but may have chicken pox, he added. "We understand she is healthy and happy and I believe, waiting to come back to her grandmother here," he said.  Watch authorities announce their find » . The journey west took them more than two thousand miles from Mansfield, the north-Central Ohio city where the girl and her mother live. "I am very happy that my granddaughter's coming home," said Mary Watson, Haylee's grandmother. "And I just want to thank all of you from the bottom of my heart." Watson, 24, and Potter, 27, were arrested without incident and held by the San Diego County Sheriff's Department. When asked their reaction, Elliott said, "I believe a little shocked that we were able to find them." Potter and Watson were still using the same vehicle, a 1980s blue Chevrolet pickup truck they drove from Ohio, Elliott said. Watson's hair was a bit darker and Potter also changed his appearance slightly. Authorities had feared Haylee was endangered. Potter, a sex offender, had escaped a half-way house on May 28, the day the girl and her mother fell out of sight. Countless tips came in while they were missing but one in particular led to the breakthrough on Tuesday, Elliott said without elaborating. But a tip from members of the ranch could have lead to the raid and arrest, a ranchmember told CNN. Kevin Carlin, a member of the ranch in the neighborhood of Valley Center, told CNN in a telephone interview that ranch members became suspicious when a former ranch guest saw billboards urging help in finding Haylee and the two adults. Elliott also praised intense national news coverage from programs such as HLN's Nancy Grace and Issues with Jane Velez-Mitchell, as well as local media and Clear Channel, which put up missing child billboards across the country. When she is returned to Ohio, Haylee will be placed in the custody of her grandmother, Elliott said. The U.S. Marshals Northern Ohio Violent Fugitive Task Force had offered a $10,000 reward for information leading to the arrest of 27-year-old Potter. Potter was wanted on a state warrant for parole violation and a federal warrant for probation violation. He is a convicted tier three sex offender, according to the U.S. Marshals Service, a unit of the Justice Department. While on the run, Potter and Watson were reportedly seen on surveillance video on May 31 at a Wal-Mart Store in Marion, Ohio, 40 miles from Mansfield. Haylee was not on that video. Adding to concerns, Watson's roommate, Samantha Covert, said last week in an interview on Nancy Grace that she saw the little girl in bed with her mother and Potter the morning they disappeared. Covert said Watson carried a basket of clothing, pillows and blankets. Watson will likely face state charges, including harboring a fugitive, according to Elliott. In addition to other charges, he said Potter may be prosecuted under the Adam Walsh Child Protection and Safety Act, a federal sex offender registration and self-reporting law that carries a multi-year felony sentence if violated. On its Web site, the Morning Star Ranch describes itself as "a community of growers of organic, pesticide-free avocados, grapefruit, persimmons, nuts, and other produce." Elliot said he believed it is a rehab facility and also called it a Christian retreat.

**Headline:** 2,000-Mile Manhunt Ends in Relief: Missing 4-Year-Old Ohio Girl Found Safe at California Retreat

**COLUMBUS, Ohio** — A harrowing, three-week cross-country search for a missing four-year-old Ohio girl came to a joyful conclusion this week when law enforcement officers located the child unharmed in Southern California, thousands of miles from her home. 

The high-stakes investigation began three weeks ago when the young girl vanished from her Ohio neighborhood. Concern quickly turned to alarm when investigators discovered that the child’s mother had absconded with her in the company of a convicted sex offender who was actively evading federal law enforcement. Given the fugitive’s criminal history, federal, state, and local agencies immediately launched a coordinated, high-priority manhunt.

For twenty-one agonizing days, detectives from Ohio worked alongside the U.S. Marshals Service and the FBI, chasing leads, reviewing security footage, and analyzing digital footprints. Despite following dozens of dead ends across multiple state lines, the trail remained cold as the trio moved undetected across the country. 

The critical breakthrough finally came early Tuesday morning, not from high-tech surveillance, but from a vigilant member of the public. After seeing a national broadcast displaying the child's photo and the fugitive’s mugshot, an alert citizen recognized the adults and contacted a local tip line. The tipster provided a precise location: a secluded, off-the-grid retreat nestled in the hills of Southern California.

Acting swiftly on the intelligence, a joint tactical team comprised of federal marshals and local California sheriff's deputies converged on the property. Fearing for the child's safety, officers executed a carefully planned, low-profile approach to secure the perimeter. 

Upon breaching the residence, authorities located the young girl hiding inside. To the immense relief of investigators, the four-year-old was found physically safe and in good health. Both the mother and the fugitive sex offender were taken into custody without incident. 

"This is the outcome every law enforcement officer prays for," said a spokesperson for the U.S. Marshals Service during a press conference. "For three weeks, our focus was singular: bring this little girl home safely. Thanks to a crucial tip from a watchful citizen and seamless inter-agency cooperation, a potentially tragic situation was averted."

The two adults are currently being held in a California detention facility awaiting extradition back to Ohio, where they face a slew of serious charges, including felony child endangerment, custodial interference, and harboring a fugitive. Additional federal charges are expected.

Social services immediately took custody of the young girl to conduct medical evaluations and provide support. Law enforcement officials confirmed that arrangements have been finalized to fly her back to Ohio, where an anxious and relieved family is eagerly awaiting her return, bringing a triumphant end to a terrifying 2,000-mile ordeal.

When tuning into a major news network like **CNN**, viewers are presented with a daily snapshot of a nation defined by its vast geographic, cultural, and political diversity. Few comparisons illustrate this contrast more vividly than the stories emerging from **California** and **Ohio**—two states that often represent opposite ends of the American political and economic spectrum.

On any given broadcast, **CNN** anchors might take viewers from the sun-drenched, tech-driven corridors of **California** to the manufacturing hubs and suburban neighborhoods of **Ohio**. 

In the West, **California** is frequently covered as a trendsetter for environmental policy, social progressivism, and economic innovation. With its massive economy—rivaling that of entire nations—the Golden State serves as a baseline for deep-blue political ideology and modern tech-culture challenges, from housing crises to climate adaptation. When **CNN** correspondents report live from Los Angeles or San Francisco, the narrative often focuses on the future of work, green energy, and national cultural shifts.

Conversely, shifting the broadcast to **Ohio** offers a compelling look at the American heartland. Long considered the ultimate political bellwether, **Ohio** has evolved in recent years, becoming a crucial barometer for Rust Belt economics, manufacturing revival, and the shifting dynamics of working-class voters. During election cycles, **CNN’s** interactive maps frequently highlight counties in **Ohio** to analyze how populist movements and economic anxieties are reshaping the political landscape. 

While **California** and **Ohio** may seem worlds apart in lifestyle, climate, and voting patterns, they remain deeply interconnected through national policy, interstate migration, and shared economic dependencies. Networks like **CNN** play a vital role in telling both stories, helping citizens in the Midwest understand the policy experiments of the Pacific Coast, while ensuring West Coast audiences stay connected to the industrial core that powers the nation. 

Ultimately, the contrast between **California** and **Ohio** isn't just a tale of two states; through the lens of national media, it is a masterclass in the complexity of modern America.

**Missing 4-year-old Haylee Donathan found safe in California; mother and fugitive sex offender in custody**

**By CNN Staff**

**(CNN)** — A multi-state search for a missing 4-year-old girl came to a relief-filled end after authorities located little Haylee Donathan safe in California, law enforcement officials announced. 

Her mother, Amber Donathan, and Robbie Potter, a convicted sex offender and fugitive, were taken into custody without incident following a coordinated operation involving local, state, and federal agencies.

Haylee, who was the subject of an urgent search across state lines, was evaluated by medical personnel and found to be in good health, according to law enforcement. She has been placed in the care of child protective services while arrangements are made to reunite her with authorized family members.

### A nationwide search ends in California

The search for Haylee intensified after authorities learned she was in the company of Potter, a registered sex offender who had active warrants for his arrest and had cut off his court-ordered monitoring equipment. Investigators believed the young girl was in "imminent danger" due to Potter's criminal background and the circumstances of her removal.

According to officials, law enforcement tracked the trio’s path from Oklahoma through several states before digital evidence and tips from the public led investigators to a location in California.

Deputies with the local sheriff’s office, working alongside federal marshals, moved in to secure the scene once the location was verified. 

"Our primary focus from the very beginning of this investigation was ensuring the safe recovery of this little girl," a spokesperson for law enforcement said during a news conference. "Thanks to the relentless work of our detectives, federal partners, and vigilant citizens, Haylee is safe today."

### Suspects face multiple charges

Amber Donathan was arrested on charges including custodial interference and child endangerment. Potter faces additional charges, including harboring a fugitive, probation violations, and charges related to his failure to register as a sex offender.

Both suspects are currently being held in a California detention facility pending extradition proceedings back to Oklahoma to face formal charges.

Authorities expressed immense gratitude to the public and the media for sharing Haylee’s story, noting that widespread public awareness was crucial in generating the leads that led to her location.

"When a child goes missing under these circumstances, time is our biggest enemy," officials added. "This outcome is the best possible news we could have hoped for."
